cards.title: 4.1 What is a Muscle
body: A muscle is made of fibres that can contract and relax. Muscles can only pull, never push, so skeletal muscles work in antagonistic pairs.

cards.title: Muscles: fuller notes
body: Together, the skeletal and muscular systems support the body and allow movement. A tendon attaches muscle to bone.

cards.title: Voluntary Muscles
body: Origin is the anchor. Insertion is the bone that moves. Biceps bends the elbow; triceps straightens it.

cards.title: Antagonistic pair: biceps and triceps
body: To bend the arm the biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes. To straighten it the triceps contracts and the biceps relaxes.

cards.title: Worked example: lifting a load
cards.problem: A student lifts a book by bending the elbow. Describe what each muscle does.

steps.text: The biceps contracts and pulls the forearm up.
To lower the book, the triceps contracts while the biceps gradually relaxes.

cards.answer: Biceps contracts to bend; triceps contracts to straighten.

cards.title: Common mistakes
head: Mistake
Correct idea
rows: Muscles only pull; a pair is needed.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Muscles only pull. Skeletal muscles work in pairs. Smooth muscle is in organ walls. Cardiac muscle never tires.

questions.q: Muscles have no function in the
why: The endocrine system works through hormones, not muscle action.

questions.q: Which types of muscles are striated?
why: Skeletal and cardiac muscle are striped. Smooth muscle is not.

questions.q: The function that is not done by voluntary muscles is
why: Peristalsis is done by involuntary smooth muscle.
